identity.real_world_identity_notes: Swift 009.c of the 1998 CART season, Swift Engineering's second CART chassis, a carbon fibre monocoque running the Ford-XD 2,650 cc V8 turbo.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: automatic cut on upshifts, no automatic blip, and a clutch needed to pull away, so the driver supplies the downshift blip.
This class runs four configurations: base, high downforce, Speedway and Superspeedway. The two oval packages are why the suffixes differ from the downforce pairs used elsewhere in the dataset.

The reviewed source gives no transmission for this chassis, so unlike its classmates the gearbox is not corroborated by a real-world specification. The controls are recorded from the drive, and the gearbox type is the sequential the drive observed rather than a sourced claim.
This car was absent from the coverage queue until it was loaded.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.swift-009c-ford-cosworth-high-downforce.20260815t223445748z-609e504b by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the chassis, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
The source establishes the chassis and engine but states no transmission, so the six sequential gears, automatic cut and absent automatic blip rest on the guided drive alone.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.
